Fit a two-level latent profile model

Source: R/multilpa.R
multilpa.Rd

Multilevel latent profile analysis describes heterogeneity among observations and among the groups they are nested in: measurements within persons, students within schools. Observation-level profiles are patterns in the indicators; group-level classes differ in how prevalent each profile is among their members. A profile has the same measurement parameters in every group class, so group classes differ only in composition.

multilpa() estimates the measurement parameters, the profile probabilities within each group class, the group-class proportions and the posterior memberships at both levels. The default is Gaussian indicators with diagonal within-profile covariances. The reported start need not have converged: read Starts and convergence before interpreting a fit.

Usage

multilpa(
  data,
  vars,
  id,
  n_profiles,
  n_group_classes = 2L,
  profile_covariates = character(),
  group_covariates = character(),
  variance_model = c("varying", "equal"),
  n_starts = 10L,
  max_iter = 1000L,
  tol = 1e-08,
  min_variance = NULL,
  seed = NULL,
  start = NULL,
  missing = c("error", "fiml"),
  profile_slopes = c("shared", "group_class"),
  covariance_model = c("diagonal", "full"),
  categorical = character(),
  min_probability = 1e-10,
  time = NULL,
  fixed = character(),
  centering = c("none", "person", "grand"),
  volume = NULL,
  shape = NULL,
  orientation = NULL,
  model = NULL,
  select_start = c("likelihood", "converged"),
  prior = NULL,
  noise = FALSE,
  acceleration = c("squarem", "none"),
  family = c("profiles", "additive", "dispersion", "additive_dispersion",
    "restricted_cross_level", "full_cross_level"),
  between_variance = c("varying", "equal"),
  weights = NULL,
  ordinal = character(),
  count = character(),
  count_model = c("poisson", "negative_binomial"),
  count_dispersion = c("varying", "equal"),
  scaling = c("none", "person", "grand"),
  drop_empty = TRUE,
  cores = 1L,
  local_dependence = character(),
  direct_effects = character(),
  search = NULL,
  n_screen = NULL,
  boundary = c("allow", "exclude")
)

Arguments

data

A data frame with the indicators and the group identifier.

vars

Names of the indicator columns. Those not named in categorical, ordinal or count are continuous.

id

Name of the group identifier column (character, factor or numeric, without missing values). id = NULL fits a single-level model in which each row is its own unit; n_group_classes must then be one.

n_profiles

Number of individual profiles.

n_group_classes

Number of group classes (default 2).

profile_covariates, group_covariates

Complete numeric columns of data that predict profile and group-class membership through multinomial logits (last class as reference), estimated in one step and entering in their own units. A group covariate must be constant within its group. See Covariates.

variance_model

"varying" (default): each profile has its own variances or covariance matrix; "equal": one shared by all profiles.

n_starts

Number of EM starts (default 10). The first is deterministic (Ward's clustering), the rest random. See Starts and convergence.

max_iter

Maximum EM updates per start (default 1000). max_iter = 0 evaluates the starts without updating them; with start, that is the model at exactly those values.

tol

Convergence tolerance (default 1e-8), per observed indicator value: EM stops when a step changes the log likelihood by no more than tol times the number of observed indicator values.

min_variance

Lower bound on every variance (on every covariance eigenvalue under full covariance). NULL (default) uses 1e-6 times the smallest sample variance of the continuous indicators, on the scale fitted; a number is an absolute bound in squared indicator units. An estimate at the bound is a boundary solution and warns.

seed

Optional integer seed. The caller's random-number state is restored on exit.

start

Optional starting values, replacing the first start: a list of means, variances (profiles by indicators), profile_probabilities (group classes by profiles), group_probabilities, and where the model has them covariances and response_probabilities (one profiles-by-categories matrix per categorical indicator). starting_values() produces one from a fit.

missing

"error" (default) rejects missing indicator values; "fiml" maximizes the observed-data likelihood under MAR, integrating the missing values out. Covariates must be complete either way. See Missing data.

profile_slopes

"shared" (default): one slope per profile logit, common to all group classes. "group_class": separate slopes in each group class, a cross-level interaction with n_group_classes times as many slope parameters.

covariance_model

"diagonal" (default): the indicators are independent within a profile; "full": within-profile covariances are estimated.

categorical

Indicators modelled by profile-specific response probabilities over their observed categories, the latent class measurement model. Binary, ordered and unordered indicators share this parameterization. Naming a subset of vars fits a mixed-mode model.

min_probability

Lower bound on every categorical response probability (default 1e-10).

time

Optional column giving each row's occasion within its group, used only to order the rows for get_results(x, "sequences"), "sequence_summary" and plot_sequences(). Values must be unique within a group and sort in their intended order (numbers numerically, factors by level, text alphabetically, so "T2", "T10" is refused: use a factor or zero-pad).

fixed

Measurement blocks held at the values in start instead of estimated: "means", "variances" (EEI, VVI, EEE and VVV only), "response_probabilities", or "measurement" for all; the mixing parameters cannot be held. A held block is not counted in n_parameters. fit_staged() runs the two-stage workflow in one call.

centering

How to centre the continuous indicators before fitting. "none" (default) fits them as supplied. "person" subtracts each group's own mean, so the profiles describe within-unit change and the group classes are types of change pattern. "grand" subtracts one mean per indicator. See Scale.

volume, shape, orientation

The covariance structure by its three components: volume "equal" or "varying"; shape "equal", "varying" or "spherical"; orientation "axis" (no covariances), "equal" or "varying". NULL (default) follows variance_model and covariance_model. The combinations are the fourteen mclust models:

volumeshapeorientationmodel
equalspherical-EII
varyingspherical-VII
equal/varyingequal/varyingaxisEEI, VEI, EVI, VVI
equal/varyingequal/varyingequalEEE, VEE, EVE, VVE
equal/varyingequal/varyingvaryingEEV, VEV, EVV, VVV
model

The covariance structure as one of those fourteen codes, such as "VVI", instead of the other structure arguments; the codes enumerate_classes() takes.

select_start

Which start is reported. "likelihood" (default): the highest log likelihood, preferring a converged start among those within the convergence tolerance of it. "converged": the best converged start when there is one. See Starts and convergence.

prior

NULL (default) for maximum likelihood, or a prior_control() object for maximum a posteriori estimation of the Gaussian means and covariances under mclust's conjugate prior, with its data-dependent defaults. See Prior and noise.

noise

TRUE adds a noise component of constant density over the data's hypervolume, which absorbs outliers and scatter no Gaussian profile explains. See Prior and noise.

acceleration

"squarem" (default) accelerates EM with SQUAREM, which never lowers the likelihood; "none" runs plain EM. Fits with prior or membership covariates always use plain EM.

family

"profiles" (default) is the model described above. The others have group classes without individual profiles ("additive", "dispersion", "additive_dispersion") or estimate profiles and group classes from the same indicators ("restricted_cross_level", "full_cross_level"). See Model families.

between_variance

For the additive, additive-dispersion and cross-level families only (an error with the others): between-group variances per group class ("varying", default) or one set shared by all classes ("equal"). The dispersion family takes "equal" only.

weights

Name of a numeric column holding a sampling weight per independent unit: per group in a two-level fit (constant within the group), per row in a single-level one. See Weights.

ordinal

Indicators modelled as ordinal (an ordered factor or integers): an adjacent-category logit with category intercepts shared by all profiles and one location per profile, Latent GOLD's default ordinal model, with (K - 1) + (C - 1) parameters per indicator against K * (C - 1) for categorical (K profiles, C categories). An unused factor level warns; drop it with droplevels().

count

Indicators holding non-negative whole numbers, modelled as Poisson with one mean per profile, or negative binomial under count_model.

count_model

"poisson" (default) or "negative_binomial" (NB2, variance mu + alpha * mu^2) for counts more dispersed than a Poisson within a profile. A dispersion estimated at zero is a boundary solution.

count_dispersion

One negative-binomial dispersion per profile ("varying", default) or one shared by all ("equal").

scaling

How to scale the continuous indicators before fitting, at the same levels as centering: "none" (default), "grand" (each indicator divided by its standard deviation over the sample) or "person" (by each group's own standard deviation). With the matching centring these are z-scores. See Scale.

drop_empty

TRUE (default) leaves rows with no observed indicator, and groups made only of such rows, out of the sample sizes, entropies and classification tables, as Mplus does, keeping their rows with NA in the assignment tables. FALSE counts them in the entropies, the tables and the number of groups, so the criteria over groups and those using the entropy change; the number of rows in the individual-level criteria stays the informative rows for profile and class models. For transition models, FALSE also counts all positive-weight rows in the individual-level BIC. Estimation is the same either way; fits with different settings are not compared.

cores

Number of processor cores for the starts (default 1); the result is identical to one core, and a covariate fit runs on one. To fit several models, give cores to enumerate_classes() instead.

local_dependence

Pairs of indicators that stay associated within each class, written "item1:item2": a within-class covariance for two continuous indicators, a joint distribution for two categorical ones (Latent GOLD's item1 <-> item2 | Cluster). See Indicator types.

direct_effects

Direct effects of covariates on continuous indicators, written "indicator ~ covariate" (several joined with +): the covariate shifts the indicator's mean by the same amount in every profile, so what it explains is not read as a profile difference; means are then at covariate zero. See Indicator types.

search

"kmeans" runs n_starts starts to convergence; "emEM" screens a pool of n_screen starts with a short EM run each and runs the first start and the best of the rest, n_starts in all, to convergence. NULL (default) is "emEM" when continuous indicators share one covariance matrix across profiles (EII, EEI or EEE) and "kmeans" otherwise.

n_screen

For search = "emEM" only, the size of the screened pool (default five times n_starts, at least n_starts).

boundary

Whether a start with a variance at min_variance may be reported: "allow" (default) does, as Mplus does, with a warning; "exclude" chooses among the other starts, and reports the best with a warning when every start is at the bound.

Value

A multilpa object: the measurement parameters, the profile probabilities within each group class, the group-class proportions, the posteriors and classifications at both levels, log_likelihood, the information criteria (bic and bic_groups on the number of groups, bic_individual on the number of rows with an observed indicator), the starts table, converged and boundary. get_results() returns its tables, parameter_inference() its standard errors and bootstrap_lrt() tests it against a nested fit.

Starts and convergence

The first start is Ward's clustering of the standardized indicators; the others are k-means from random centres, or under search = "emEM" a screened pool that also holds random partitions. get_results(fit, "starts") lists every start. The reported start is the one select_start picks; converged says whether it converged, and summary() says how many starts replicated its log likelihood. A replicated likelihood does not establish a global optimum. With profile-specific variances the highest likelihood can belong to a nearly degenerate profile on a few observations: a variance at min_variance warns, boundary = "exclude" sets such starts aside, and get_results(fit, "gaussian_diagnostics") describes each profile's support. Wald inference is refused for a fit that did not converge or has a parameter at its bound.

More than one group class needs more than one profile and a group with more than one row; a model of categorical and ordinal indicators with more free parameters than its table has free cells warns. Neither check establishes identification. Labels are arbitrary.

Missing data

Under missing = "fiml" EM uses the observed-data likelihood; only the initialization fills missing values with means. A row with no observed indicator contributes no measurement likelihood but receives posteriors from its group, and drop_empty governs how it enters the reported statistics. Missing patterns can prevent identification.

Covariates

Naming profile_covariates or group_covariates fits the one-step covariate model (class multilpa_covariates), with profile intercepts per group class, slopes shared unless profile_slopes = "group_class", and Wald standard errors from parameter_inference(). With start and fixed = "measurement" from a fit without covariates, only the logits are estimated: the two-step estimator, whose criteria and standard errors condition on the held measurement. three_step() and r3step() are the staged alternatives. A covariate model does not take prior, noise, direct_effects or a continuous local_dependence pair.

Indicator types

Continuous indicators are Gaussian within profiles; categorical, ordinal and count indicators are independent of each other and of the continuous ones given the profile. Ordinal and count indicators work with FIML, weights, two-level fits, covariates, inference, predict() and lta(), but not with start, fixed, prior, noise or the other families. A categorical local_dependence pair becomes one indicator over the combinations of its categories; an unobserved combination sits on the min_probability floor and still counts as a parameter. local_dependence is not combined with the structure arguments (covariance_model, model, volume, shape, orientation), time, prior, noise or held variances, and a continuous pair not with covariates either; direct_effects needs a diagonal covariance and complete covariates, and is not combined with membership covariates, continuous pairs, time, prior, noise, fixed, start, centering or scaling. The tables "ordinal", "count_means", "local_dependence" and "direct_effects" of get_results() hold the estimates.

Scale

Centring and scaling are applied before fitting and stored on the fit, so get_results() returns the supplied data and predict() transforms new units the same way. Estimates, likelihood and criteria are on the fitted scale, so only fits with the same centring and scaling are comparable. Grand scaling changes only the units under a structure unchanged by rescaling each indicator (EEI, VEI, EVI, VVI, EEE, VEE, EVV, VVV) and changes the solution under the others. Person centring needs each group observed more than once on each indicator, and refuses singly observed indicators even when other groups have repeats; person scaling also needs variation within the group, and a group observed exactly twice is flagged as uninformative. Grand offsets and scales use sampling weights when supplied. Grand scaling divides by the population standard deviation (observed weight in the denominator); person scaling uses the within-group sample standard deviation.

Weights

The fit maximizes the pseudo log likelihood sum(w_j * log(L_j)), the weights scaled to sum to the number of units of positive weight as Mplus does, so integer weights act as repeated units. A unit of weight zero changes nothing, enters no statistic, and keeps its row and posterior in the assignment tables. Standard errors are sandwich estimates (vcov_type = "robust"); the bootstrap resamples units with their weights. Weights work with every family, covariates, categorical indicators and FIML; bootstrap_lrt(), three_step(), r3step(), prior and noise refuse a weighted fit.

Model families

Three group-class-only families: each group has a Gaussian intercept per indicator drawn from its class's distribution, and its members vary around it. "additive": classes differ in means (and in between-group variances under between_variance = "varying"), with one within-group variance per indicator; "dispersion": in within-group variances; "additive_dispersion": in both. They take only data, vars, id, n_group_classes, between_variance, n_starts, max_iter, tol, min_variance, seed, weights, search and n_screen, need complete continuous indicators, and return a multilpa_additive fit with summary(), plot(), Wald inference, enumerate_classes() by family and bootstrap_lrt() across numbers of group classes. They are experimental: no bootstrap inference, FIML, covariates or discrete indicators.

Two cross-level families estimate profiles and group classes from the same indicators, each group's indicator means being between-level indicators of its class: "restricted_cross_level" holds the profile prevalences equal across classes and estimates the levels separately; "full_cross_level" lets them differ. They take data, vars, id, n_profiles, n_group_classes, variance_model, between_variance, n_starts, max_iter, tol, min_variance, seed and weights, have no standard errors, and return a multilpa_cross_level fit whose likelihood is computed on the same scale only between cross-level fits of the same data. It counts the ratings twice, once directly and once through their group means, so its criteria favour group classes and the full form even on data with no group structure: they do not choose the number of group classes or the form, and a fit with group classes warns with class latents_cross_level_criteria.

Prior and noise

prior is available for EII, VII, EEI, VEI, EVI, VVI, EEE, EEV, VEV and VVV with complete continuous indicators and without fixed or covariates; the mixing proportions have no prior. As in mclust, the likelihood and criteria are unpenalized values at the posterior mode; Wald inference is not defined there, and the bootstrap refits each resample with the same prior.

noise is available for complete continuous indicators with one group class, under any structure, with or without prior, and not with fixed or covariates. The component's density is 1 / V, with V mclust's hypvol(), and it adds two parameters; a supplied start includes noise_probability. It is profile 0 in the classification: subject_profiles is 0 there, the assignment table has posterior_noise, and the posterior and profile-probability tables have profile-0 rows, while the measurement tables describe the Gaussian profiles only. Inference, the three-step functions, bootstrap_lrt(), starting_values(), fit_staged(), bivariate residuals and the posterior plots refuse a noise fit.

Every refusal above is a classed condition; latents-conditions lists them.

See also

multilca() for a model in which every indicator is categorical; lpa() for a single-level model; enumerate_classes() to compare numbers of profiles and group classes.

Examples

# Course sessions nested in students: engagement profiles of sessions, and
# classes of students that differ in how often they are engaged.
activity <- c("browse", "lectures", "forum_read", "forum_post", "attendance")
fit <- multilpa(course_engagement, activity, "student",
                n_profiles = 2, n_group_classes = 2, n_starts = 4,
                seed = 42)
summary(fit)
